answer: The default is already set: global_settings.py defines FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS = 0o644.

models.FilePathField already supports a callable `path`: `formfield()` resolves it with `self.path() if callable(self.path) else self.path`, and `deconstruct()` stores `self.path` unchanged. A callable is therefore written into migrations as a reference, not as a path resolved on the machine running makemigrations.

SQLCompiler.get_order_by() computes `without_ordering = self.ordering_parts.search(sql)[1]` for duplicate detection; the `ordering_parts` regex (compiler.py:41-44, now with re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL) must span multiline SQL, otherwise only the last line is compared.

Media.merge in django/forms/widgets.py now uses a TopologicalSorter over all lists at once (instead of pairwise merging), so unrelated files don't impose false order constraints; the warning only fires on a real CycleError.
sqlmigrate sets self.output_transaction = migration.atomic and connection.features.can_rollback_ddl, so BEGIN/COMMIT is only emitted when the database supports transactional DDL.
The DurationField "invalid" error message already uses the corrected format "[DD] [[HH:]MM:]ss[.uuuuuu]", in DurationField.default_error_messages in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py.

The fix is already in the code. Both validators in django/contrib/auth/validators.py (ASCIIUsernameValidator at line 10 and UnicodeUsernameValidator at line 20) use r"^[\w.@+-]+\Z". The trailing `$` was replaced with `\Z`, so a trailing newline is rejected. The leading `^` is fine because the flags don't include MULTILINE.

HttpResponseBase.make_bytes in corpus/django/http/response.py already handles memoryview. Its isinstance check on `(bytes, memoryview)` returns `bytes(value)`, so `HttpResponse(memoryview(b"My Content")).content` gives `b'My Content'`. I only read the code and didn't run it.

The fix is already in this codebase. In the single-instance fast-delete path of `Collector.delete()`, line 456 runs `setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None)` after the delete query. That sets the instance's PK to None. The line numbers in the report (276-281) point at `collect()`, which only queues fast deletes, so the PK reset belongs in `delete()`.

The fix is in iter_modules_and_files() in django/utils/autoreload.py. It special-cases the `__main__` module (manage.py), which often has no `__spec__`. It adds `module.__file__` to the watched paths instead of skipping the module. Without this, manage.py was never watched.

The fix is in auth/migrations/0011_update_proxy_permissions.py, in update_proxy_model_permissions. The Permission update that moves proxy permissions to the proxy content type is wrapped in transaction.atomic with `except IntegrityError`. When permissions for the proxy model already exist, the migration prints a warning instead of crashing with a duplicate key error. I read the code but did not run the migration.

Django already handles this in LazySettings: __getattr__ calls _add_script_prefix for MEDIA_URL and STATIC_URL. It prepends get_script_prefix() (the SCRIPT_NAME) to relative values. Absolute paths and http(s) URLs are left unchanged.

The fix is in `iter_modules_and_files` in django/utils/autoreload.py. It wraps `path.exists()` in `try/except ValueError`, logs the error at debug level and skips the file. Network filesystems can return null bytes in paths, so `path.resolve()` could otherwise raise "ValueError: embedded null byte" intermittently. The guard sits at lines 159-167, just before `path.resolve().absolute()` on line 168. I haven't reproduced the error or run anything.

The models.E028 check in check_all_models now emits a warning (models.W035) instead of an error when settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS is configured, so the same db_table in different apps/databases is allowed. The error is only raised when no routers are configured.

The check already exists. Field._check_choices in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py works out the longest string value in choices. If it is longer than max_length, it returns the error fields.E009: "'max_length' is too small to fit the longest value in 'choices' (%d characters)." The error is built at the cited line.

The fix is in `get_caller` in django/views/debug.py. `technical_404_response` calls it to find the view name. When `request.resolver_match` is None, `get_caller` calls `resolve(request.path)` again. If a path converter's `to_python` raises Http404, that second call raises it again. Before the fix, nothing caught it, so the technical 404 page crashed and the server returned the plain "A server error occurred" text. Now `get_caller` wraps the call in `try/except Http404: pass` and returns an empty string when there is no match, so the technical 404 page renders. I read the code but did not run it.

EnumSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py serializes enum members by name (f"{module}.{enum_class.__qualname__}[{item.name!r}]"), producing Status['GOOD'] instead of Status('Good').
The check is already in the code. `IsNull.as_sql` in `lookups.py` raises `ValueError("The QuerySet value for an isnull lookup must be True or False.")` when the right-hand side isn't a `bool`.

The two-digit year check is in `parse_http_date` in `corpus/django/utils/http.py`. It already compares against the current year instead of using the hard-coded 0-69 / 70-99 split. The check is `if year - (current_year % 100) > 50:` (line 121). A two-digit year more than 50 years ahead is put in the previous century. Any other two-digit year goes in the current century.

The fix is the `Choices.__str__` method in django/db/models/enums.py. It returns `str(self.value)`, so a Choices member set on a model instance now casts to its value (e.g. "first") instead of "MyChoice.FIRST_CHOICE". `IntegerChoices` and `TextChoices` both inherit it from `Choices`. I read the code and didn't run the question's tests.

The code that overrides the inner query's GROUP BY is in `Exact.get_prep_lookup`. When the rhs is a sliced subquery, it calls `clear_select_clause()` and `add_fields(["pk"])` on it. That swaps the selected column for the pk, and the GROUP BY is then rebuilt from it, so the query groups by `id` instead of `email`. In this corpus that block is already guarded by `if not self.rhs.has_select_fields:`. `set_values()` sets `has_select_fields = True`, so a query that went through `.values('m')` skips the rewrite. I did not run the example, so I haven't confirmed that this guard stops the bug. The corpus may already contain the fix, and I picked this line as the best match.

Field.contribute_to_class used to set get_FOO_display unconditionally, which replaced a user-defined override. In this code it only sets the method when "get_%s_display" % self.name is not already in cls.__dict__. The check is at this line, and the setattr is on lines 952-956. A method defined on the model class itself is therefore kept. Methods inherited from a parent are not checked, so overriding inherited choices still works.

In MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields (django/db/migrations/autodetector.py), the ForeignKey branch handles renamed to_field by resetting new_field.remote_field.field_name to the old field's name (old_field.remote_field.field_name), which yields the stale to_field='field_wrong' in the AlterField.

The SQLite DatabaseCreation.test_db_signature must include the TEST NAME (not just settings NAME) for file-based test DBs so distinct aliases with persistent test DB files aren't treated as the same database (otherwise they share/lock the same DB). See django/db/backends/sqlite3/creation.py test_db_signature: the `sig.append(test_database_name)` branch for non in-memory DBs.

In RegexPattern.match, `args = () if kwargs else match.groups()` is computed from the unfiltered `groupdict()`, before None-valued kwargs are removed. This line is the fix for the reported crash. In the buggy code, `kwargs` was filtered first, so the unmatched optional group left it empty. `args` then fell back to `match.groups()`, which passed the extra positional arguments and caused the TypeError. Here the code already guards against this. I haven't run it against the example URLconf.

The bug came from the check in Field.contribute_to_class that decided whether to install get_FOO_display. It used `hasattr(cls, 'get_%s_display' % self.name)`, which is also true when the method is inherited. So the child class never got its own method bound to its own field and choices. The code now checks `cls.__dict__` instead, so only a method defined directly on the class is kept, and an inherited one is overridden. I haven't run the example from the report to confirm it.

Field.deconstruct builds the path from `self.__class__.__qualname__` instead of `__name__`. That makes an inner class serialize as `module.Outer.Inner` rather than `module.Inner`. It is in `Field.deconstruct` in `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py`.

I didn't run a reproduction. The check I did do: this checkout already has the `__qualname__` fix in `Field.deconstruct`.

A second place also uses `__qualname__`: `Field.__repr__` at line 264. That one only affects the displayed name, not migrations.

The enum case (`test1.models.State` instead of `test1.models.Thing.State`) goes through the migration serializer, not `Field.deconstruct`. I only read the function serializer there, which also uses `__qualname__`. I didn't read the part that handles class values like `State`, so I can't say whether that case is fixed too.

The fix is already in place. `check_language_settings_consistent` in `django/core/checks/translation.py` calls `get_supported_language_variant(settings.LANGUAGE_CODE)` and returns E004 only if that raises `LookupError`. That function, in `django/utils/translation/trans_real.py`, falls back to the base language (for example `de` for `de-at`), so E004 is no longer raised when only the base language is available. I didn't run it. I only read the code.

The fix is already in the code. `deserialize_db_from_string` wraps the object loading in `atomic(using=self.connection.alias)`, so forward references and cycles are handled. It also disables constraint checks inside that block.

display_for_field in django/contrib/admin/utils.py has a special case for models.JSONField that returns json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, cls=field.encoder) (falling back to display_for_value on TypeError), so readonly JSON shows as valid JSON.

The wrong hint (E334/E335 in ManyToManyField._check_relationship_model) is already corrected in this code. The hint now reads 'If you want to create a recursive relationship, use ManyToManyField("self", through="...")' instead of ForeignKey(..., symmetrical=False, through=...). Both occurrences are in corpus/django/db/models/fields/related.py, at lines 1550-1551 (E334) and 1571-1572 (E335).

The fix is the `name != "pk"` condition in `find_ordering_name`. Without it, `Child`'s `pk` (the `parent_ptr` relation) was treated as an ordinary relation. The compiler then expanded it into `Parent.Meta.ordering` (`-pk`) and lost the descending direction, so the query came out ASC. With the condition, `pk` is ordered directly and keeps its DESC direction. The condition is already in this code. I only read the code and did not run the query.

SafeExceptionReporterFilter.cleanse_setting in django/views/debug.py only recursed into dicts and returned other iterables (lists/tuples) as-is; the fix adds recursive cleansing of list and tuple values (elif isinstance(value, list) / tuple branches).

The GROUP BY handling for Subquery annotations is in Query.get_group_by_cols (sql/query.py), which returns [wrapper or self] when external cols are possibly multivalued, together with set_group_by (query.py:2252-2253) which groups by Ref(alias, annotation) -> `GROUP BY "status"`, ambiguous with the joined ab.status column. Subquery.get_group_by_cols (expressions.py:1584) delegates to this.

The crash comes from `SchemaEditor._delete_composed_index()` in `django/db/backends/base/schema.py`. It raises `ValueError("Found wrong number (%s) of constraints ...")` whenever `len(constraint_names) != 1`. `alter_index_together()` calls it with `{"index": True, "unique": False}`. That filter is meant to skip the `_uniq` constraint on the same columns, so only the `_idx` one is found. In the code here, the `unique=False` check in `_constraint_names()` (line 1867) does that skipping. The failure in the report happens when the lookup matches both the `_uniq` and `_idx` constraints, which gives 2 matches. I did not run a migration to reproduce it.

In Collector.delete (django/db/models/deletion.py), the counter only records a model label when count is non-zero (`if count:` guards in the fast_deletes loop and in the instance delete loop), so zero deletions return (0, {}) consistently for both simple and FK models. The fast-delete branch at line 474 is where simple models' zero count was previously recorded as {label: 0}.

QuerySet.distinct() calls self._not_support_combined_queries("distinct"). That helper raises NotSupportedError ("Calling QuerySet.distinct() after union() is not supported.") when the query has a combinator.

The check is already in `Model._check_constraints`. It collects `constraint.fields` and `constraint.include` from every `UniqueConstraint` into a set. It then passes that set to `cls._check_local_fields(fields, "constraints")` at base.py:2529. That call raises models.E012 for nonexistent fields, E013 for many-to-many fields, and E016 for non-local fields. I read the code but didn't run it or test it against the demonstration.

The line I'm submitting is where the `UniqueConstraint` field names are gathered.

The fix is already in the code. StaticFilesHandlerMixin defines `async def get_response_async(self, request)`. It runs `self.serve` through `sync_to_async` and turns `Http404` into a response with `response_for_exception`. I didn't run anything to confirm it fixes the traceback.

slugify() in django/utils/text.py already strips leading and trailing dashes and underscores. The return line is `re.sub(r"[-\s]+", "-", value).strip("-_")`, and the docstring says the same. With that line, "___This is a test ---" gives "this-is-a-test". I read the code but did not run it.

The `check_filterable` method in `Query` reads the `filterable` attribute from any object passed as the RHS of a filter. A model instance with a `filterable=False` field therefore looks like a non-filterable expression, and the method raises NotSupportedError. The fix is the guard `hasattr(expression, "resolve_expression")`, which limits the check to real expressions. It is already in this code at the line below.

In SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name, the related model's default Meta.ordering is applied when the ordered field is a relation, unless its attname matches the last piece of the order_by name. The old code compared attname to the whole `name` (e.g. "record__root_id"), so `order_by("record__root_id")` never matched. It then followed the relation, added the extra self-join, and used OneModel's "-id" ordering. That is why the sort came out DESC, and why "-record__root_id" came out ASC (the "-" flips the inherited "-id"). The comparison against `pieces[-1]` at line 1054 is the fix. I did not run the queryset to confirm.

Query.set_empty() adds a NothingNode to the query's where clause and now also calls set_empty() on every query in self.combined_queries. Without that loop, QuerySet.none() on a union()/intersection()/difference() only emptied the outer query, and the combined sub-queries still returned all their rows. QuerySet.none() (query.py:1424) calls it.

ValidationError.__eq__ is already defined in django/core/exceptions.py. It returns NotImplemented for non-ValidationError objects and otherwise compares hash(self) == hash(other). The matching __hash__ makes the comparison independent of error order. For a single error it hashes (message, code, params). For an error dict it hashes the dict made hashable. For an error list it hashes a tuple of the errors sorted by message.
The syndication view already passes comments to feed.add_item(), using self._get_dynamic_attr("item_comments", item). No further change is needed in views.py.

The duplicates came from applying limit_choices_to as a plain join filter. `apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield` in `corpus/django/forms/models.py` now avoids that. It wraps the limit_choices_to condition in `Exists(...)` with `Q(pk=OuterRef("pk"))` instead of calling `complex_filter` on the queryset. The join can then no longer repeat rows. The `Exists` filter is applied at line 131. I did not run anything or check the regression test.

SessionBase.decode catches BadSignature and any other Exception (e.g. binascii.Error: Incorrect padding) and returns an empty session dict instead of crashing; the legacy decode fallback no longer exists.

Field.__eq__ in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py compares creation_counter and the field's model, so abstract-inherited fields on different models are unequal. __lt__ orders by creation_counter first, then by model. __hash__ (line 690) still hashes only creation_counter and has not been changed to include the model.

The autodetector already handles this case. In `generate_created_models`, the `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` operation is added at line 703, before the `AddIndex` operations at line 719. This is the ordering the report asks for, so a new `CreateModel` no longer puts `AddIndex` on `_order` ahead of `AlterOrderWithRespectTo`. I didn't run a migration to confirm, and I didn't check how the operations are sorted afterwards.

`AddIndex` has no explicit dependency on the `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` operation. It depends only on the related fields and the model itself, so the ordering comes from the order the operations are added in.

The separate path in `generate_added_indexes` (line 1307) is for models that already exist. I did not find a dependency there either, so adding an `_order` index to an existing model could still be ordered wrongly.

PasswordResetTokenGenerator._make_hash_value() in django/contrib/auth/tokens.py now includes the user's email in the token hash. It looks up the email with user.get_email_field_name() and falls back to an empty string if the user has none. A token issued before an email change therefore no longer validates.

The model class is already added to the app_list context. `_build_app_dict` puts it in each model's dict under the `"model"` key (`"model": model`). `_build_app_dict` is still private. Only `get_app_list` calls it, in this file.

In serialize_db_to_string's get_objects (django/db/backends/base/creation.py), the `app_config.label in loader.migrated_apps` check is wrong when TEST MIGRATE is False: MIGRATION_MODULES is restored before serialization, so the loader treats apps (e.g. admin) as migrated and tries to serialize tables that were never created (syncdb'd without migrations). Fix: remove the MigrationLoader / migrated_apps condition.

Query.resolve_lookup_value in django/db/models/sql/query.py already handles this. For namedtuples (detected by `_make`), it rebuilds the value with `type_(*values)`, which expands the resolved elements. Other list and tuple types still use `type_(values)`.

ManagementUtility.execute already passes prog=self.prog_name to CommandParser, so the fix described in the ticket is already in the code. The call is at line 366 and the `prog` argument is on line 367.

The bug is in `handle()` in `shell.py`. It calls `exec(options["command"])` with no globals dict, so functions defined in the `-c` code can't see names imported by that same code. The stdin branch has the same problem. In this checkout the `-c` call at line 117 already reads `exec(options["command"], globals())`, which looks like the fix (upstream Django used that form). The stdin call at line 127 is `exec(sys.stdin.read(), globals())`. I did not run anything to confirm the behaviour.

In `InlineModelAdmin.__init__`, when `verbose_name_plural` is None and the inline sets `verbose_name`, it is now built from that name with `format_lazy("{}s", self.verbose_name)`. If the inline sets neither, it falls back to the model's `Meta.verbose_name_plural`. The code in the repo already contains this behaviour, so I made no changes.

The bug is in `KeyTransformIsNull.as_oracle` in `corpus/django/db/models/fields/json.py`. For `isnull=True` it returns `(NOT has_key OR lhs IS NULL)`. The extra `lhs IS NULL` branch also matches rows where the key exists with JSON null. The fix is to return just `NOT has_key` for `isnull=True`, and drop the `lhs IS NULL` part at lines 465-467.

`as_sqlite` (lines 469-477) already uses `JSON_TYPE(%s, %%s) IS NULL`. That returns the string 'null' for a JSON null, so it shouldn't match those rows. I haven't run any tests to confirm either point.

Signal.send_robust() logs receiver exceptions through the `_log_robust_failure()` helper. The helper calls `logger.error(..., exc_info=err)` on the "django.dispatch" logger. `send_robust()` calls it from its `except Exception` clause for sync receivers, and the async receiver wrapper does the same.

ModelChoiceField.default_error_messages['invalid_choice'] is a fixed string with no %(value)s placeholder: "Select a valid choice. That choice is not one of the available choices." To fix it, change the message to "Select a valid choice. %(value)s is not one of the available choices." Then pass params={'value': value} where the field raises ValidationError with code 'invalid_choice'. That raise is in ModelChoiceField.to_python/validation, and I did not open it.

The W042 warning is emitted by Model._check_default_pk in django/db/models/base.py. The fix for inherited PKs is the exclusion of models whose pk is a OneToOneField parent_link (inherited PKs are checked in parent models), so child models with multi-table inheritance don't warn.

The fix is in Model._prepare_related_fields_for_save (django/db/models/base.py). It now checks `getattr(self, field.attname) in field.empty_values` rather than `is None`. When the related object was saved after assignment, the parent's empty-string FK (`product_id=""`) is therefore refreshed from the related object's pk with `setattr(self, field.name, obj)`.

Q._combine rejected non-Q operands (`if not isinstance(other, Q): raise TypeError(other)`), so Q() & Exists(...) failed. The fix is to accept any conditional expression: `if getattr(other, "conditional", False) is False: raise TypeError(other)`, with the empty-Q case returning `other.copy()`. Combinable.__and__ already handled Exists & Q.

The crash comes from `Q._combine`, which used to deep-copy the other operand when one side was empty. Deep-copying `dict_keys` raises the pickle error. In this codebase `_combine` already avoids it. For an empty `Q()` it returns `other.copy()`, and `self.copy()` in the other empty case. `Node.__copy__` in `django/utils/tree.py` is shallow and reuses `self.children`, so the `dict_keys` value is never copied.

I read the code but did not run `Q() | Q(x__in={}.keys())`. The line below is where the shallow copy replaces the deepcopy.

ResolverMatch.__init__ never unwraps functools.partial. A partial has no `__name__`, so the check at line 65 treats it like a class-based view. `_func_path` then becomes "functools.partial". `__repr__` (lines 79-80) works around this by printing `repr(self.func)`. The fix is to unwrap `func.func`, and keep `func.args` and `func.keywords`, in `__init__` before this check, so the repr shows the underlying function and its arguments.

AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__ must use issubclass(subclass, self._subclasses) instead of `subclass in self._subclasses`. That way subclasses of BigAutoField and SmallAutoField pass the check. The code at this line already does this, so the fix is in place in this corpus.

ReadOnlyPasswordHashWidget.id_for_label returns None, so BoundField.label_tag (django/forms/boundfield.py:190-192) leaves out the "for" attribute. The widget already has this override in the codebase.

The directory-name validation for startapp is in TemplateCommand.handle in django/core/management/templates.py. In this version it calls validate_name(os.path.basename(top_dir), "directory"), where top_dir = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(target)). abspath normalizes the path and drops the trailing slash, so basename no longer returns ''. This is the line the issue is about, and it is already fixed here; the original bug was basename(target) on the raw path. I read the code but did not run django-admin startapp to confirm.

BoundWidget.id_for_label now returns self.data["attrs"].get("id"), so it uses the id set by ChoiceWidget.options. It no longer builds 'id_%s_%s' from the name and index. The code in this corpus already has the fix, so I made no change.

FormSet.full_clean already creates non-form errors with error_class="nonform" (the initial _non_form_errors ErrorList, and again at line 458 when a ValidationError is caught), mirroring the "nonfield" class used in forms.py.

Handled in Query.add_deferred_loading (django/db/models/sql/query.py): when deferring removes all names from the "only" set (existing.difference(field_names) is empty), it calls clear_deferred_loading() and then sets the remaining new names as deferred (new_only, True), so only("name").defer("name") selects just the pk instead of all fields.

The fix is already in the code. `ManyToManyRel.identity` wraps `through_fields` in `make_hashable(self.through_fields)`, so a list value no longer breaks `hash(self.identity)`. I didn't change anything or run the repro.

The check is in ManyToManyField's `_check_ignored_options`. It adds a warning, fields.W345, when `self.remote_field.symmetrical and self._related_name` is true. The warning reads "related_name has no effect on ManyToManyField with a symmetrical relationship, e.g. to "self".". It is a `checks.Warning`, not an error. The condition itself is on line 1443.

The refactor is already in the code. AutocompleteJsonView.get() builds its results by calling self.serialize_result(obj, to_field_name). The new serialize_result() method returns {"id": str(getattr(obj, to_field_name)), "text": str(obj)}. Subclasses can override it to add extra fields.

The fix is already in this code. In `_multi_decorate`, `bound_method = wraps(method)(partial(method.__get__(self, type(self))))` copies `__name__`, `__module__` and the other wrapper assignments from `method` onto the partial. Decorators like `logger` that use `func.__name__` therefore no longer fail with the AttributeError.

The `models.Model` special case in `TypeSerializer.serialize` is the cause. It must return the import `from django.db import models` along with the string "models.Model". Without that import, a `bases` tuple like `(app.models.MyMixin, models.Model)` is written without the import, and the migration fails with the `NameError`.

In this checkout the entry already carries the import, so the fix appears to be in place. I did not reproduce the bug.

`MigrationWriter.as_string` in `writer.py` (line 172) then merges that import into `from django.db import migrations, models`. I read the writer and the sequence serializers and found nothing else that would drop the import.

get_admin_url in django/contrib/admin/helpers.py passes current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name to reverse(). That makes the readonly ForeignKey link resolve under the custom admin site rather than /admin/.

ModelChoiceIteratorValue defines __eq__ but, in the broken version, no __hash__, which makes instances unhashable. The fix is to add `def __hash__(self): return hash(self.value)`, which is already present in this code.

The fix belongs in RenameModel.database_forwards. It currently has no check for an unchanged table name. When old and new models share an explicit db_table, it still calls alter_db_table and then alter_field on every related field. That is what drops and recreates FK constraints on Postgres and rebuilds the table on sqlite. I haven't edited the code or run anything. The change would be to compare old_model._meta.db_table with new_model._meta.db_table right after old_model is fetched (line 438) and return early if they match.

MultiWidget.id_for_label (in corpus/django/forms/widgets.py) is the method the issue wants removed. In this corpus it already returns "" (so no `for` index is generated), but it is still defined on the class at line 937 rather than removed.

URLValidator.__call__ in django/core/validators.py calls urlsplit(value), which can raise ValueError ("Invalid IPv6 URL"). The fix is to wrap it in try/except ValueError and raise ValidationError. That wrapper is already in the code at lines 125-128. I did not run the reported example to confirm it now raises ValidationError.

The crash comes from `Col.relabeled_clone` in `django/db/models/expressions.py`. The remake renames the table references, which calls `Expressions.rename_table_references` and then `relabeled_clone({old_table: new_table})` on the constraint's expressions. Without a guard, that gives alias-less columns a table alias, so the SQL becomes `"new_table"."name"`. SQLite rejects the "." operator in index expressions.

The guard is already in this tree: `if self.alias is None: return self`. The constraint's `Query(..., alias_cols=False)` makes `final_transformer` in `query.py` (line 1799) produce `Col(None, ...)`, and the guard keeps those columns unqualified when relabeling. I didn't run the migration, so I haven't confirmed the crash is gone.

ExpressionWrapper.as_sql compiles the inner expression with no handling for FullResultSet. For ~Q(pk__in=[]), the WhereNode raises FullResultSet because the negated empty match is always true. Nothing catches it, so the SELECT column is rendered as empty SQL ("SELECT AS foo"). The fix is to catch FullResultSet in ExpressionWrapper.as_sql and compile Value(True) instead. NegatedExpression.as_sql already handles EmptyResultSet in a similar way.

The bug is in `template_changed` in `django/template/autoreload.py`. With BASE_DIR in `TEMPLATES[0]['DIRS']`, every file under the project counts as being inside a template directory, including `.py` files. The handler then calls `reset_loaders()` and returns True. Returning True tells the autoreloader the change was handled, so it skips the restart. The fix is the early return at lines 49-50, which ignores `.py` files so a Python change still triggers a restart. That check is already in this copy of the file, so this copy already contains the fix. I read the code but did not run the repro.

SimpleLazyObject.__radd__ is implemented using @new_method_proxy: it calls the wrapped object (after _setup if needed) and returns `other + self` (wrapped). Defined at the __radd__ method in django/utils/functional.py.

RenameIndex.database_backwards in corpus/django/db/migrations/operations/models.py returns early (a no-op) when old_fields is set, i.e. for an unnamed unique_together index. So the index keeps its new name and is never restored to its old auto-generated name. In get_conditional_response, the If-Modified-Since value is only parsed when it is non-empty. The same guard is already in place for If-Unmodified-Since at lines 171-173. The code at this line already looks like the fix, and I didn't change or run anything.

BaseCommand.create_parser sets the parser's formatter_class via kwargs.setdefault("formatter_class", DjangoHelpFormatter). A command can pass its own formatter there. DjangoHelpFormatter is a plain HelpFormatter subclass that only reorders arguments, so the description gets rewrapped.

The check collects libraries from TEMPLATES['OPTIONS']['libraries'] and from installed apps into one dict. The false E003 comes from that dict storing paths in a list. A library registered in OPTIONS and also found in an app's templatetags is then counted twice, even though both paths are identical. The fix is to collect the paths in a set, `defaultdict(set)` with `.add()`, so identical paths are de-duplicated and only genuinely different modules trigger the error. The code in the repo already does this; I read it but did not run it.

The autodetector already handles this case. EnumSerializer in django/db/migrations/serializer.py serializes a combined Enum flag value by splitting it into its member flags and joining them with " | ". It uses list(self.value) on Python 3.11+ and enum._decompose on older versions. Each member is written as module.Class['NAME'].

The IndexError comes from `if str_number[0] == "-":`. When the number is None (a null field), `str(number)` is "None", and for an empty string it is "", so indexing [0] fails. The fix is to use `str_number.startswith("-")` or check `if str_number and str_number[0] == "-"`.

The hidden initial input (`initial-<name>`) used with `show_hidden_initial` (set for callable defaults in `Field.formfield`) was re-rendered with the current bound value, so after a failed submit the "initial" became the user's data. A second submit then compared data against itself, so `has_changed()` returned False and the inline was treated as empty and dismissed. `BoundField.as_widget` now handles this: when `only_initial` is set and the hidden initial name is in the form data, it propagates the submitted hidden initial value instead of `self.value()`.

The wrong object comes from the FilteredRelation branch of get_related_selections() in compiler.py. It builds klass_info with a "local_setter" that calls final_field.remote_field.set_cached_value(from_obj, obj). For a multi-level path such as pool__tournament__pool, final_field is the last hop's field, so that setter caches the filtered-relation object on the wrong instance. The guard that avoids this is `partial(local_setter, final_field) if len(joins) <= 2 else local_setter_noop`. It uses the real setter only for single-hop relations and a no-op for longer paths. That guard is already in this corpus, so I could not find the bug elsewhere. I did not run the test case, and this answer is based on reading the code only.

The `join` filter in corpus/django/template/defaultfilters.py only escapes the joining string when `autoescape` is on. With `autoescape` off it does a plain `arg.join(value)` (line 601), so the separator is not escaped.

The check is in `QuerySet._batched_insert()`. It keeps `returning_fields` only when `bulk_return and (on_conflict is None or on_conflict == OnConflict.UPDATE)`. Otherwise it calls `_insert()` without `returning_fields`. The `OnConflict.UPDATE` case is what lets `bulk_create(update_conflicts=True)` return IDs on backends that support it, such as PostgreSQL. `ignore_conflicts` still goes to the `else` branch, so no IDs are returned there. The compiler then adds the RETURNING clause in `SQLInsertCompiler.as_sql()` (compiler.py, around lines 1775-1797).

The squash handling is in `CreateModel.reduce`, in the `RenameIndex` branch. When a `RenameIndex` has `old_fields`, it removes the matching entry from the `index_together` option. It also adds a `models.Index(fields=old_fields, name=new_name)` to `indexes`. The squashed `CreateModel` therefore no longer carries `index_together`, so the deprecation warning goes away. The branch starts at line 344.

In the reverse one-to-one branch of `get_related_selections`, `select_related_descend` is called with `related_select_mask` (the related model's own mask) instead of the parent `select_mask`. The call is at lines 1254-1260, and the wrong argument is on line 1258.

Inside `select_related_descend`, the check `field not in select_mask` is therefore made against the wrong mask. The forward-relation call at line 1211 passes `select_mask` correctly. I read the code and did not run it or change anything.
